liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half Step** (2 reviews): Its opening strains eased the reviewer's tension after the disappointing previous night; Reviewer hears Jerry already reaching for the skies in the opener [14][15]
- **Gentlemen Start Your Engines** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the song is about drinking rather than cars, and wishes the band had played it more; Reviewer says this Brent song could have been skipped, and groups it with other Brent songs that interrupt strong sets [10][12]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer says it doesn't smoke but sizzles [15]
- **Push Comes To Shove** (1 review): Reviewer says Brent's tinkling keyboard work lifts it above the mundane [15]
- **Black Muddy River** (1 other source): The uploader's list places Black Muddy River as the encore [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Cumberland Blues**: cut on the recording [21]
- **Gentlemen Start Your Engines**: rare: 3 archived performances [21]
- **See You All Later**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-06-26.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.115733.Flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 127 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1988-06-26.163568.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 133 min [3]
- **gd88-06-26.sbd-matrix.nawrocki.5608.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 125 min; rated 3.89/5 by 18 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the sound quality of this show pretty average; Reviewer says this recording sounds far better than the low-quality tape they previously owned; Reviewer praises the recording as a soundboard/audience mix that keeps good sound quality and some of the room's feel [13][16][17]
- **gd1988-06-26.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.115734.Flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 127 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Floor seats were taken by the soundboard, so the band had the reviewer reseated in the first row off the floor, Phil's side [14]
- This was the reviewer's third Dead show, and the one where they understood what seeing the band live meant [16]
- Reviewer was born on the day of this show and enjoys hearing what was played then [19]
- This was the last of about 50 Dead shows the reviewer saw, put off by crowds after the In The Dark album [20]
- The previous day at Buckeye was unremarkable, with an odd sound mix that didn't feel like the usual Dead [14]
- Reviewer considers it a strong Brent show with a prominent mix and a really good summer 88 show [17]
- Reviewer felt the band was losing joy and fire again, after fabulous performances the previous year [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-06-26.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.115733.Flac1644**: taped by Floater; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Nakamichi CM300/CP4 Shotguns>Sony D5; Taper Floater,Transfer By Keo; Tapes Maxell XL-II 90's; Transfer With Nakamichi MR-1>Korg MR-1000 @ 1… [1]
- **gd1988-06-26.163568.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME80 mics > Sony D5M [3]. Also: A Schoeps CMC4 MK2 source from Greg Clark and Charlie Miller supplies an 11-second patch in Cumberland Blues; The same Schoeps source also supplies a 28-second patch in Space [3]
- **gd88-06-26.sbd-matrix.nawrocki.5608.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD/Matrix > Dat > CDR > Sonic Solutions > CDR > EAC > CDWave > mkwACT [6]
- **gd1988-06-26.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.115734.Flac2496**: taped by Floater; transferred by Keo; source: Mast er Audience Nakamichi CM300/CP4 Shotguns>Sony D5 Taper Floater,Transfer By Keo Tapes Maxell XL-II 90's Transfer With Nakamichi MR-1>Korg MR-1000 @ 1… [2]
